DELETE this entry when #3313 lands — the stale-entry check fails until it is removed.

REAL, UNFIXED. `WORD_CHAR_RE = /[\p{L}\p{N}]/u` drives CommonMark `_`-flanking; a combining mark is neither letter nor digit, so on NFD text the base letter of an accented cluster reads as a word edge and emphasis flanks in the wrong place. Adding `\p{M}` changes markdown parse/serialize behaviour and needs round-trip + conformance coverage, so it is tracked as follow-up rather than slipped into a CI-guard PR.

REAL, UNFIXED. `HUMAN_TAG_RE = /(^|[^\p{L}\p{N}_])#([\p{L}\p{N}_][\p{L}\p{N}_/-]*)/gu` rewrites pasted user content, and its boundary/name classes exclude combining marks, so `#café` in NFD form splits mid-grapheme. It must stay byte-identical to its Rust twins (HUMAN_TAG_RE in src-tauri/src/commands/pages/markdown.rs and the same literal in src-tauri/src/commands/pages/inline_query_md.rs), so the fix is a coordinated FE/BE change plus conformance vectors — tracked as follow-up.

Cited by #3348. `categorizeHistoryError` classifies a `listPageHistory` failure by substring-matching the lower-cased error message against English fragments (`fetch`, `timeout`, `internal server`, `sqlx`), which are locale- and version-dependent. The structured probes it tries first (`status` 5xx, `code` matching ^5xx) are the correct mechanism; removing the substring fallback requires the backend to return a stable machine-readable error code, which is out of scope for this guard PR.

REAL, UNFIXED, low severity. `WORD_RE = /[\p{L}\p{N}_]/u` backs the whole-word in-page find; on NFD text a trailing combining mark is read as a word boundary, so whole-word `cafe` matches inside `café`. This path only paints highlight ranges (visible, transient) — it never rewrites stored content — so it is tracked as follow-up rather than fixed here.
